title: Manual Loop Unrolling (Compiler Defeat)
pattern: Manually expanding a loop's iterations into consecutive sequential statements to avoid the overhead of branch evaluation or index incrementing.
why_bad: It defeats compiler loop optimizations, increases the binary instruction size (resulting in L1 instruction cache misses), and prevents the compiler from performing architecture-specific vectorization. Straightforward loops are easier for optimizing compilers to optimize [338, 347, 348].
detection: Look for a series of consecutive statements that perform identical operations on sequential array indices or loop variables, where a simple `for` loop or iterator could be used.
counterexample: In extremely low-level hard real-time graphics rendering or embedded microcode where manual assembly unrolling has been profiled and proven necessary on a specific CPU. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 2, Section 2.5 (p. 23); *Code Complete*, Chapter 25.3 (p. 338, 347, 348).
